critiques.summary: H1 (ledger-db storage exhaustion, independent of v6.0.0) is the best-supported origin and the round-1 blocking gap is now closed: disk_used_pct was actually measured and rises smoothly and monotonically from 78.16% at 11:00Z to 100% at ~14:54-14:56Z, then stays pinned at exactly 100.0% through 16:28Z with no reclaim step — a gradual, ~9h pre-existing ramp that precedes the 15:00Z onset and is not deploy-aligned (F31/F32/F33). The failure signature is unambiguously storage-layer ('could not extend file'/'pg_wal xlogtemp: No space left on device', 292 ledger-db errors F21, 179/179 payment-service ERROR logs F8), the blast radius is shared-DB-shaped (payment 60.65%, settlement 53.56%, api-gateway 16.43% in the same 15:00Z bucket, F10), and the rollback at 15:12Z changed nothing (F22/F23). H2/H3 are positively killed: untruncated full-window log queries returned zero MANDATE_HOLD/enum/unknown-entry-type/constraint matches in either service (F19/F20), and the mechanism (constraint rejection) cannot produce a storage error or take down services that never run the mandate flow. H4 (neighbour write-flood into the same shared DB) is not positively refuted, but its load-growth hop is unfalsifiable with the accessible toolset (no per-writer write/QPS metric exists — F26/T6), and every available proxy contradicts it: no writer changed near onset (F27/F28), disk ramp has no load-like inflection (F32), and connections/CPU/slow-queries are flat (F34/F35). H4 therefore remains a weaker, untestable alternative rather than a competing origin deserving another round; the discriminating evidence does not exist. Confidence capped at 0.85 because the exact growth mechanism (retained WAL vs base-table/autovacuum) is unpinned and H4 cannot be formally excluded. Acceptance also flags a timeline inconsistency (F1/F6/F11/F13 place onset ~15:00Z, before the 14:46Z deploy, vs the reported '~15 min after release' and F11's '15:25 rollout') — the core conclusion (onset independent of the deploy) is robust to it, but the reported timeline should be corrected.

challenges.issue: The growth mechanism behind the 21.8pp ramp (retained WAL from an inactive replication slot vs base-table/relation growth vs autovacuum) is never pinned: no pg_wal size / archive-backlog / replication-slot metric exists in available_metrics (only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min). The WAL interpretation rests on log message strings plus a rising replication_lag (F36), not on a size measurement. This does not change the origin (ledger-db storage exhaustion) but leaves the precise fill driver an assumption.

H4's defining hop — a non-payment writer increasing write/transaction volume near 15:00Z — remains entirely unverified, and the metric that would test it does not exist in the accessible toolset (F26, T6). It is kept as a ranked alternative only because it shares H1's storage-exhaustion mechanism and blast radius; absent any measurable writer-rate data it can be neither confirmed nor excluded. Every available proxy (no writer deploy/config change F27/F28, no connection surge F34, flat CPU/slow-queries F35, smooth no-inflection disk ramp F32) contradicts rather than supports it.

Timeline inconsistency: F1/F6/F11/F13 place the error onset at ~15:00Z, which is BEFORE the 14:46Z v6.0.0 deploy, while the report claims onset '~15 minutes after the release' and F11 references a '~15:25 rollout'. The 14:46Z deploy time with a 15:00Z onset is internally inconsistent with the reporting. The conclusion that onset is independent of the deploy is stable either way, but the incident summary should state the corrected timeline.

Blast radius is incomplete: order-service error_rate was never queried (tool budget), so whether the fourth ledger-db writer is also a co-victim is unconfirmed. This would strengthen the shared-storage origin but does not change the ranking since three writers plus api-gateway already establish the shared-DB signature.
